facts.statement: The genus Cymatosaurus was first described by Fritsch in 1894.
Cymatosaurus belongs to the family Cymatosauridae.
Cymatosaurus is classified within the superorder Sauropterygia.
Cymatosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropterygian that is either a pistosauroid or a nothosauriform.
facts.quote: Cymatosaurus is an extinct genus of pistosauroid or nothosauriform sauropterygian.

facts.statement: Cymatosaurus lived during the Early Triassic to the Middle Triassic, specifically from the latest Olenekian to the Anisian stages.
facts.quote: It is known to have been alive from the Early Triassic to the Middle Triassic period (latest Olenekian to Anisian stages)

facts.statement: Fossils of Cymatosaurus have been found in Germany, and the genus likely originated in the Netherlands.
facts.quote: of Germany and they seem to originate from the Netherlands.

facts.statement: Cymatosaurus was small to medium-sized for its group, reaching lengths of 1 to 1.2 meters.
facts.quote: It was small to medium-sized for an eosauropterygian, measuring 1 - 1.2 m long.

facts.statement: Cymatosaurus is an extinct genus of pistosauroid sauropterygians.
facts.quote: Cymatosaurus es un género extinto de sauropterigios pistosauroides.

facts.statement: Cymatosaurus appeared in the early Triassic and disappeared in the middle Triassic, distributed across Germany and the Netherlands.
facts.quote: Apareció en el periodo Triásico temprano y desapareció en el Triásico medio (en las últimas etapas del Olenekiense y Anisiense), se distribuía en Alemania y los Países Bajos.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Cymatosaurus is Pistosauroidea.
